inputs.research_question: Should Tata Power enter the commercial EV fast-charging market in Rajasthan in FY27?

events.summary: Client strategy documents and 3-year financials retrieved
Deloitte Research Methodology DEL-RM-2026 loaded
Methodology Section 5.3 — Market Entry Evidence Thresholds identified as binding

policy_reference.title: Market Entry Evidence Thresholds
policy_reference.text_excerpt: A market entry recommendation requires three independent demand-side sources and a validated competitor cost baseline; otherwise the engagement must be escalated for partner review.
policy_reference.application: Three demand-side sources are available, but the competitor cost baseline has conflicting figures — full-scale entry cannot be recommended yet.

events.summary: State EV policy and tariff data evaluated — charging margins viable

evidence.title: Rajasthan EV Policy 2024 and Tariff Orders
evidence.content_summary: Per-kWh charging tariff capped at ₹1.10; charging stations classified as a licensed activity with simplified approvals.
evidence.relevance: Establishes the regulatory cost base for the charging-margin model

events.summary: Third-party market outlook evaluated — 34% CAGR forecast

evidence.title: EV Charging Infrastructure Outlook 2026
evidence.content_summary: Forecasts 34% CAGR for commercial fast-charging demand in western India through FY30; utilisation is the dominant profitability driver.
evidence.relevance: Primary demand-side source for the pilot-scale estimate

events.summary: Competitor cost baseline reviewed — conflicting figures found

evidence.title: Competitor Benchmark Set (4 operators)
evidence.content_summary: Per-kWh prices across the four benchmarked operators vary by 22% between the two compiled sources; two figures could not be reconciled.
evidence.relevance: Competitor cost baseline fails the Section 5.3 validation threshold

decision.outcome_summary: Conditional recommendation: enter via a phased pilot in the Jaipur–Udaipur corridor. Demand-side evidence supports pilot scale, but the competitor cost baseline is contested — full-scale entry is deferred pending verification (Methodology Section 5.3).

structured_rationale.primary_reason: Demand-side sources triangulate to a viable pilot scale and the regulatory cost base is favourable, but the competitor cost baseline fails the validation threshold in Section 5.3, so a full-scale entry recommendation cannot be defended yet.
supporting_factors: Three independent demand-side sources agree on pilot-scale volumes
State tariff cap and simplified licensing improve unit economics
Competitor price figures vary by 22% across sources and remain unreconciled
exclusions_applied: Section 5.3: Full-scale entry deferred — competitor cost baseline unverified

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Recommending full-scale entry on an unverified cost baseline breaches Section 5.3
Demand-side evidence is strong; declining the pilot ignores a validated opportunity

inputs.research_question: Is Velm Robotics a viable automation partner for the Bhiwandi fulfilment centre?

events.summary: Vendor registry and financials retrieved
Deloitte Research Methodology DEL-RM-2026 loaded
Methodology Section 6.1 — Red-Flag Escalation identified as binding

policy_reference.title: Red-Flag Escalation
policy_reference.text_excerpt: A vendor exhibiting two or more diligence red flags (litigation history, financial distress, unverifiable references, sanction exposure, IP disputes) must be rated conditional and routed for partner sign-off.
policy_reference.application: Vendor exhibits 2 of 5 red flags — conditional rating and partner sign-off are required before contract award.

events.summary: Litigation database check reviewed — two pending disputes

evidence.title: Court Records Search — Velm Robotics
evidence.content_summary: Two pending commercial disputes filed 2025–2026, both relating to delayed system deliveries.
evidence.relevance: Counts toward the Section 6.1 red-flag threshold

events.summary: Audited financials reviewed — receivables ageing doubled

evidence.title: Velm Robotics FY25 Financial Statements
evidence.content_summary: Revenue growth of 41%, but receivables ageing doubled year-over-year and the auditor flagged going-concern assumptions.
evidence.relevance: Financial-distress indicator counting toward the red-flag threshold

decision.outcome_summary: Recommendation: proceed with caveats — 2 of 5 diligence red flags unresolved; partner sign-off required before contract award.

structured_rationale.primary_reason: Two red flags (litigation history, financial-distress indicators) are open under Section 6.1, so the vendor is rated conditional and the recommendation cannot be issued without partner sign-off.
supporting_factors: Two pending commercial disputes in public court records
Receivables ageing doubled year-over-year with a going-concern note
Technical capability scores from the evaluation team remain strong
exclusions_applied: Section 6.1: Partner sign-off required — 2 red flags open

inputs.research_question: What is the addressable export market for agricultural spraying drones in Southeast Asia?

events.summary: Client brief and engagement scope retrieved
Deloitte Research Methodology DEL-RM-2026 loaded
Methodology Section 1.2 — Independence and Conflicts Restriction identified as binding

policy_reference.title: Independence and Conflicts Restriction
policy_reference.text_excerpt: Advisory work for a client whose direct competitor is an existing audit client of the firm is prohibited without an approved independence waiver.
policy_reference.application: The market leader in the target segment is an existing audit client of the firm — no waiver is on file.

events.summary: Conflict register extract reviewed — audit-client overlap confirmed

evidence.title: Firm Conflict Register Extract
evidence.content_summary: AgriNova's largest regional competitor has been an audit client of the firm since FY23; no independence waiver is recorded for advisory work in the same market segment.
evidence.relevance: Directly triggers the Section 1.2 independence restriction

decision.outcome_summary: Not recommended: engagement declined — Section 1.2 independence restriction applies because the segment leader is an existing audit client of the firm and no waiver is on file.

structured_rationale.primary_reason: Advising AgriNova in a segment where the firm audits a direct competitor is prohibited by Section 1.2 without an approved independence waiver, and no waiver exists — any deliverable would create a firm-level independence breach.
supporting_factors: Conflict register confirms an active audit relationship with the segment leader
No independence waiver is on file for this market segment
Scope reduction would not cure the conflict because the overlap is client-level
exclusions_applied: Section 1.2: Engagement declined — independence conflict with existing audit client

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: A reduced-scope study does not cure a client-level independence conflict

scenarios.case_type: Pricing Benchmark Study — D2C Personal Care

inputs.research_question: What launch price band should GlowRoot use for its new face-serum line in modern trade?

events.summary: Client category data and historical pricing retrieved
Deloitte Research Methodology DEL-RM-2026 loaded
Methodology Section 3.4 — Secondary Source Triangulation identified as satisfied

policy_reference.title: Secondary Source Triangulation
policy_reference.text_excerpt: Pricing recommendations must triangulate at least two independent retail-audit panels and reconcile any variance above 8% before publication.
policy_reference.application: Three retail audit panels agree within a 4% variance band — the triangulation threshold is met.

events.summary: Retail audit dataset evaluated — panels agree within 4%

evidence.title: Retail Audit Dataset — Q2 FY26 Personal Care
evidence.content_summary: Panel data across modern trade shows the ₹349–₹399 band captures 62% of premium face-serum volume; inter-panel variance is under 4%.
evidence.relevance: Establishes the recommended price band within the Section 3.4 variance threshold

decision.outcome_summary: Recommended: launch price band of ₹349–₹399 validated across three retail audit panels within a 4% variance.

structured_rationale.primary_reason: Three independent retail audit panels triangulate within the 4% variance allowed by Section 3.4, and the ₹349–₹399 band covers the majority of premium volume, so the pricing recommendation is fully defensible.
supporting_factors: All three audit panels agree within a 4% variance band
Band covers 62% of premium face-serum volume in modern trade
Client cost structure supports a 58% gross margin at the midpoint

inputs.research_question: Is Voltaic Mobility a viable acquisition target for BlueOrbit Fund III?

events.summary: Target data pack and 2-year screening history retrieved
Deloitte Research Methodology DEL-RM-2026 loaded
Methodology Section 8.4 — Deal-Stopping Findings identified as binding

policy_reference.title: Deal-Stopping Findings
policy_reference.text_excerpt: Screening must be withheld and the finding routed to Deal Risk Advisory where an undisclosed regulatory investigation, sanction exposure, or governance irregularity is identified.
policy_reference.application: An undisclosed consumer-protection investigation plus governance irregularities meet the deal-stopping criteria — screening is withheld pending risk review.

events.summary: Data room legal folder reviewed — undisclosed regulatory investigation found

evidence.title: Data Room — Legal Correspondence Folder
evidence.content_summary: Correspondence shows an open consumer-protection authority investigation into battery certification claims, referenced in an NDA annex but absent from the disclosure schedule.
evidence.relevance: Undisclosed regulatory investigation — a deal-stopping finding under Section 8.4

events.summary: Corporate registry check reviewed — governance irregularities noted

evidence.title: Registrar of Companies Filings — Voltaic Mobility
evidence.content_summary: Two director resignations within 90 days and a declined statutory auditor re-appointment; filings show conflicting registered office addresses.
evidence.relevance: Governance irregularities corroborate the deal-stopping assessment

decision.outcome_summary: Escalated to Deal Risk Advisory: an undisclosed regulatory investigation and governance irregularities meet the deal-stopping criteria in Section 8.4 — screening is withheld pending risk review.

structured_rationale.primary_reason: An undisclosed consumer-protection investigation, corroborated by registrar filings showing governance irregularities, satisfies the deal-stopping criteria in Section 8.4 — the screening recommendation is withheld and the finding routed to Deal Risk Advisory.
supporting_factors: Investigation referenced in an NDA annex but absent from the disclosure schedule
Two director resignations within 90 days; auditor re-appointment declined
Deal value of ₹420 crore elevates the materiality of any undisclosed liability
exclusions_applied: Section 8.4: Screening withheld pending Deal Risk Advisory review

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Proceeding on an undisclosed investigation creates firm and client liability
Investigation is not yet conclusive — premature rejection forecloses a potentially viable deal
